messages:
ellen.k: Heads-up — we've been seeing a spike in PCIe reset events + soft ECC drift on a subset of cards in rack-west-6 since last Friday. Thought I'd surface the pattern here.

rajiv.p: Can you paste the short log snippet? Is this Xid or NVLINK flaps?

ellen.k: Mostly Xid 43/31-ish and a rising soft ECC counter. Not NVLINK. sample from node r-w6-13: 
```
[ 2026-03-12T03:21:11Z ] nvidia: pcie reset 0000:3b:00.0: link down
[ 2026-03-12T03:21:11Z ] nvidia: Xid (31): PID 4219:
[ 2026-03-12T03:21:12Z ] gpu-monitor: soft-ecc-count: 12 -> 27 in 2h
```

maria.s: That's a pretty fast jump. Any shared vendor/serial on that rack?

ellen.k: Yeah — pulled inventory: most affected cards are from serial range SN-B3K4-1000..SN-B3K4-1075, shipped Q4. Same vendor firmware rev 4.2.1.

noah-oncall: tagging @infra-bot for incident tracking and @rajiv.p for triage.

infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1842 — "r-w6 intermittent PCIe resets + soft ECC drift". Priority: P2.

rajiv.p: Quick checks: are we seeing host-side power complaints or PCIe enumeration errors? Could be power-delivery or a firmware edge.

ellen.k: Host logs show repeated AER messages and PCIe link retrain, but PSUs in rack are within normal. GPU firmware matches across lot. No recent BIOS updates.

maria.s: Do we have capacity impact? Any scheduled jobs failing?

ellen.k: Some training batches hit OOM/retry after Xid. Affected hosts are automatically drained when Xid count > 15 in 1h by our drain script, so capacity loss ~6% in us-west-2 cluster during peak. Estimated lost GPU-hours: ~42 GPU-hours since Friday.

rajiv.p: Plan proposal: 1) Quarantine serial range at rack level in inventory and mark as non-schedulable unless pinned. 2) Run coordinated safe drain of affected nodes during low-traffic window (tomorrow 01:00-03:00 UTC). 3) Collect full vendor logs and escalate for RMA / FW investigation. 4) Instrument new metric: transient-ecc-rate per-minute to catch drift earlier.

noah-oncall: +1. Also propose temporary lowering of the drain threshold from 15 -> 8 until we verify — prevents noisy retries. Thoughts?

maria.s: Lowering threshold will increase drains and cost but reduces customer-visible errors. Agree for the short window.

ellen.k: Fine with lowering threshold to 8 for 24h after drains. We'll revert after vendor provides guidance.

rajiv.p: I'll prepare the node list and a drain schedule. Basic drain command we use: 
```bash
# safe drain
infractl node drain r-w6-13 --grace 900 --migrate-jobs
```

ellen.k: Also adding a lightweight health prober to periodically poll ECC counters and PCIe AER counts: we'll push as a daemonset to the infra namespace. If prober sees ecc_delta > 5 in 30m, it emits a high-priority alert.

maria.s: Who owns the vendor escalation? @rajiv.p?

rajiv.p: I'll own it. Need dataset: serial list, full dmesg, nvidia-smi -q, vendor fw. Can someone gather and upload to the INC ticket?

ellen.k: Uploading node manifests + nvidia-smi outputs for affected nodes now. Example nvidia-smi snapshot: 
```
GPU 0: A40 Serial: SN-B3K4-1012
Product Name: A40
Driver Version: 540.2
Persistence: Enabled
ECC Errors (volatile): Corrected: 0, Uncorrected: 0
Power: 310W
```

noah-oncall: Any impact to Dedicated customers? We should check pinned capacity pools first.

ellen.k: Dedicated pools are isolated, only a spillover job from autoscaler briefly attempted to use two nodes before drain hit. No SLA violations yet but close call.

rajiv.p: Vendor reply loop: they asked for run-level microcode logs and whether the failures are correlated with long-running tiled attention loads. Anyone confirm?

maria.s: We ran longer transformer loads on the affected hosts — yes some correlation. Could be a stress-triggered firmware corner.

ellen.k: Tentative timeline: tonight we flip drain threshold to 8; tomorrow 01:00 UTC we drain 8 nodes in r-w6 and replace with spare nodes from r-west-spares; collect vendor logs; then hold for vendor analysis.

rajiv.p: RMA/next steps: if vendor confirms batch defect we'll quarantine serials, request cross-ship replacements, and run firmware rollback test on a single card to see effect. Also propose adding a procurement check to reject that vendor fw rev for now.

maria.s: Cost note — cross-ship + node replacement will add estimated $3k immediate logistics + ~120 GPU-hours of lost capacity during swap window. Flagging to finance for chargeback.

noah-oncall: I'll add a short customer-facing blurb in incidents if we see any SLA exposure.

ellen.k: After-drain checklist: run 48h soak on replacement nodes with synthetic tiled-attention load; monitor transient-ecc-rate; keep drain threshold at 8 for 24h.

rajiv.p: I'll attach a short automation to auto-tag nodes from that serial range as "quarantine" in inventory so they aren't scheduled.

ellen.k: Thanks — if anyone sees new nodes in other racks with same serial pattern, ping this thread.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-1842 updated: nodes drained: r-w6-13,r-w6-14,r-w6-19,r-w6-22,r-w6-23,r-w6-26,r-w6-28,r-w6-31. Replacements scheduled at 2026-03-15T01:00Z.

maria.s: Good work. Keep cadence updates here and we'll slot a postmortem once vendor answers. :eyes:

ellen.k: Will write up a short RCA draft after vendor response. Initial root cause hypothesis: firmware + manufacturing lot interaction causing PCIe link retrains under sustained tiled-attention workloads, leading to transient ECC drift and higher Xid incidence.

noah-oncall: Thanks team — monitoring closely.
